back: A lipid made of one glycerol and three fatty acids joined by ester bonds.

front: Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid?
back: Ester bond, formed by condensation (water released).
Saturated: no C=C, straight chains, pack tightly (solid fats). Unsaturated: C=C bonds kink chains (oils).

front: Energy per gram: lipid v carbohydrate?
back: Lipid about 37–39 kJ/g; carbohydrate about 16–17 kJ/g.
Energy store, heat insulation, buoyancy, protection of organs, metabolic water, electrical insulation (myelin).
Glycerol + two fatty acids (hydrophobic tails) + phosphate group (hydrophilic head).

front: Why do phospholipids form bilayers in water?
back: Hydrophilic heads face water on both sides; hydrophobic tails face inwards away from water.

front: Water released when one triglyceride forms?

back: An organic molecule insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents such as ethanol.
